South Surrey White Rock Ocean View Homes: streets and boundaries

items.t: This page covers view homes off the waterfront: upland benches and slopes above Semiahmoo Bay in Ocean Park (Surrey) and on White Rock's hillside streets.
Ocean Park's view lots sit on the bluff above Boundary Bay; a 2026 Surrey report describes 12588 16 Avenue as a bluff site overlooking the 1001 Steps Greenbelt and Boundary Bay.

blocks.text: South Surrey White Rock Ocean View Homes: the housing stock

items.t: View stock here is detached houses sited for elevation — bluff-edge and hillside lots — rather than the flood-level houses on the Crescent Beach flats.
The bluff lot the City documents is 2,698 square metres (about 0.27 hectares) at 12588 16 Avenue, with Kwomais Park, the closest natural area, about 400 metres walking distance in the City's report.

blocks.text: South Surrey White Rock Ocean View Homes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Steep-slope rules are the main Surrey control: the Hazard Lands Development Permit Area (DPA) covers parcels with slopes over 20% gradient, or within 10 metres downslope or 30 metres of the top of such a slope.
Its stated purpose is to protect people, property and the environment from development on unsafe slopes, and prevent soil erosion there.
A tree can decide whether a view survives: Surrey Tree Protection Bylaw, 2006, No. 16100 requires a permit for protected trees, including trees over 30 cm diameter at breast height.
White Rock hillside lots follow different documents: Zoning Bylaw, 2024, No. 2506, the OCP Schedule C Environmental DPA map, and Tree Protection Bylaw 2407.

blocks.text: South Surrey White Rock Ocean View Homes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Surrey requires two replacement trees for every permit-sized tree removed, and states fines for removing a tree can be up to $20,000.
An arborist report is required with a Surrey tree cutting application for five or more trees, and the permit must be posted on site before removal.

blocks.text: South Surrey White Rock Ocean View Homes: development and new projects

items.t: 12588 16 Avenue, Ocean Park bluff, Surrey application 7925-0012-00: a house and coach house, rezoning R3 to R2-O (Oceanfront Residential Zone, Part 14A), with Hazard Lands (Steep Slopes) permit and a variance. STATUS: planning report May 11, 2026, recommending public notification; read 2026-11-03.

White Rock OCP update: council reporting lists Draft OCP Amending Bylaw No. 2511 (OCP Update 2025) and September 2026 Bylaw 2593, including a North Bluff Corridor Plan update. STATUS: in council process as listed; read 2026-11-03.

blocks.text: South Surrey White Rock Ocean View Homes: costs and taxes

items.t: A rebuilding Surrey upland buyer also meets tree costs before a building permit: $108 plus $42 per tree, $550 per replacement tree, up to $15,000 per lot in securities.

blocks.text: South Surrey White Rock Ocean View Homes: getting around

items.t: Upland White Rock and Ocean Park are served from White Rock Centre: TransLink routes 321 (Surrey Central Station) and 351 (Bridgeport Station) run through the upland streets, with White Rock stops mainly on Johnston Road, Thrift Avenue and Oxford Street.
Fifteen stops on routes 321 and 351 are located within the City of White Rock, per the City's Zoning Bylaw 2506 corporate report.

blocks.text: South Surrey White Rock Ocean View Homes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check slope first: Surrey's Development Permit Areas page is the lookup for whether a parcel contains slopes over 20% gradient or sits in the top-of-slope or downslope buffers.
A lot can sit in more than one Surrey DPA; the City states only one permit application is then required, but not what a geotechnical report will conclude.
Check White Rock's OCP Schedule B (updated October 2024) and Schedule C (October 2017) maps for a hillside lot — check current.

faq.q: Does buying a view home protect the view?
faq.a: What is regulated is building and trees: Surrey controls siting on slopes through the Hazard Lands DPA, and its Tree Protection Bylaw, 2006, No. 16100 requires a permit before a protected tree — including one blocking a view — can be cut.

faq.q: Can I build or add on an Ocean Park bluff lot?
faq.a: Expect a geotechnical step first. The City's 2026 report for 12588 16 Avenue required a Development Permit for Hazard Lands (Steep Slopes), and the geotechnical report submitted was peer reviewed before staff found it conformed to the Official Community Plan.

faq.q: Which secondary school serves an upland address here?
faq.a: Check the exact address. Surrey School District No. 36 (SD36) states the catchment school is determined by where the address falls within the district's School Boundaries Map, using its School Locator tool; Semiahmoo Secondary, one of the South Surrey secondaries, is at 1785 148 Street.

faq.q: Can I add a suite or coach house to a house in South Surrey White Rock?
faq.a: BC's small-scale multi-unit housing rules allow more homes on many urban lots, but each municipality sets the details and many lots are excluded. Check the lot's zoning with the municipality before you plan a suite or coach house.

faq.q: Do I need a home inspection when buying in South Surrey White Rock?
faq.a: It is strongly recommended. Make the offer subject to an inspection so a qualified inspector can look at the roof, structure, drainage, electrical and heating before you remove conditions.
